quote.text: The first principle is that you must not fool yourself — and you are the easiest person to fool.
quote.author: Richard Feynman, Caltech commencement address, "Cargo Cult Science" (1974)

stories.headline: The Truce Breaks a Second Time, and This Time the Strikes Land Inside Iran
stories.dek: A week after hitting an island in the strait, American forces struck targets on the Iranian mainland — Bandar Abbas and Chabahar. Tehran called its reply a "decisive operation" and said US bases were now the target. Brent held above ninety-one dollars; neither side has drawn an off-ramp.

stories.headline: The Chipmaker Reaches for the Warehouse Everyone's Chips Ship From
stories.dek: Nvidia is reported to be buying Hugging Face — the neutral repository from which AMD, Intel and cloud accelerators all download their open models — for around thirteen billion dollars. It is a deal, not yet an announcement, and the objection is obvious the moment you name what the hub is.

stories.kicker: The Long Read · The Undercurrent · Thailand
stories.headline: The Recession-Proof Gods
stories.dek: As Thailand posts its weakest growth in thirty years, its under-thirties are pouring money and screen-time into amulets, fortunes and lucky colours — and the state and Chinese capital are both racing to industrialise the anxiety. Belief has become the one thing a stalling economy can still manufacture and export.

stories.headline: Three Days to Change Your Mind on a Loan You Just Signed
stories.dek: From 15 September, a licensed moneylender's unsecured loan comes with a cooling-off window: cancel inside three business days and you owe no interest, only a capped slice of the approval fee. It is real protection — for the better-behaved half of the market.

stories.headline: The Whole Bag Is Decided at the Zipper
stories.dek: A daily-driver pack lives or dies on six things — fabric, coating, zipper, hardware, stitching, suspension — and a good one costs about S$300. Above that you buy country-of-make and romance; below it, "genuine leather" and a no-name zip that dies in a year.

stories.headline: The Biggest Open Model of the Week Fits No Desk on Earth
stories.dek: Tencent's new Hunyuan preview is open, Apache-licensed, and enormous: nine hundred gigabytes just to hold its weights. The model a home rig can actually load is the small one — and the deal on the previous page is why the distinction has teeth.

stories.headline: The Glasses That Left the Camera Out on Purpose
stories.dek: Even Realities' G2 puts a monochrome heads-up display in a thirty-five-gram frame that looks like eyewear — and carries neither a camera nor a speaker at all. At US$599 it sells privacy as an omission, and stakes out the opposite corner from the translation glasses we flagged last week.

stories.headline: Thirty of Them, One Counter, and a Dial the Colour of Nagano in Spring
stories.dek: Grand Seiko's peach-pink Spring Drive is the kind of object that stops a page — a textured seasonal dial on a titanium 62GS case. It is also made in thirty pieces for a single American boutique, which is the honest part of the story: scarcity, priced as craft.

stories.headline: Sixteen Years Later, Erykah Badu Hands the Whole Record to a Producer
stories.dek: "Before the World Blows" is Badu's first proper album since 2008, a full collaboration with The Alchemist and a guest list from Steve Lacy to Westside Gunn. The early notices are glowing — and the honest reading is that "glowing" is resting, so far, on very few reviews.

stories.headline: The Secondary-School Dip Is Real, Normal, and Usually Passes
stories.dek: A hundred-thousand-record study finds that when a child moves up to secondary school, their wellbeing drops across the board — and that the fall tracks the move itself, not just growing up. The useful news for a parent: it is common, and it is not, by itself, a warning sign.

stories.headline: A Coin-Toss September, and Gold Falls While the Dollar Rises
stories.dek: Kevin Warsh spent Jackson Hole insisting inflation is not beaten, and the market flipped from a near-certain September cut to a real chance of a hike. Add an oil jolt from Hormuz, and the through-line is one broken pairing: gold and the dollar moving in opposite directions, with the jobs report the next referee.

stories.headline: The Camera That Sees What Your Eye Cannot
stories.dek: Deep-sky astrophotography is not really photography — it is a form of computation, dozens of exposures stacked to pull colour and structure out of a sky that looks black. It is also the hobby a $999 box just rewrote, and the one Singapore has to cheat to do at all.

stories.headline: Ninety Minutes a Week, and Nothing Waiting Past Two Hours
stories.dek: A thirty-year study of nearly a hundred and fifty thousand adults puts the strength-training sweet spot at ninety to a hundred and twenty minutes a week — and finds no extra benefit beyond it. Pair it with cardio and the death-risk number roughly halves. The ceiling is the point.

stories.headline: A Stadium Autumn, and Tokyo Leaves to Book the Flights Around
stories.dek: The season stacks up fast: Coldplay in Tokyo this week, a Grand Prix adding its first-ever Sprint, and a string of stadium nights — with Japan's autumn illuminations and a Fukuoka basho for the reader who plans the trip, not just the ticket.
